page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-288 is a high-density, compute-focused server powered by x86_64 Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors. The instance provides 288 dedicated vCPUs spanning 144 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz, supported by 504 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory totals 576 GB, resulting in a lean allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Advanced instruction support is extensive, incorporating AVX-512 vector extensions, AMX matrix acceleration, and hardware cryptography features such as VAES and SHA-NI. The server includes no integrated GPUs and has no local ephemeral storage, relying on external network-attached volumes for data persistence.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional multi-threaded computational capabilities. In multi-core stress-ng tests and PassMark CPU metrics, the instance ranks within the top tier of evaluated hardware, complemented by top-tier results in software compilation with Clang and ray tracing routines. Single-core results show moderate performance in stress-ng and text processing, while single-core Geekbench metrics maintain high tiers. Memory throughput is a significant operational strength, achieving large-block uncached read speeds exceeding 1,000 GB/sec and write rates near 448 GB/sec. Network static web throughput and in-memory key-value operations with Redis both register in the upper decile of benchmarked platforms.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory configuration delivers high processing density without allocating excess system RAM, presenting a cost-efficient architecture for parallel CPU-bound compute tasks. The lack of onboard NVMe drives and discrete GPUs marks a clear operational tradeoff, directing high-IOPS storage and graphics-dependent workloads to alternate families. The instance is specifically suited for high-throughput batch processing, extensive code compilation farms, scientific simulations, ray tracing rendering tasks, and high-concurrency static web serving.
